messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failure report shows that SystemUtils.getJavaVersionAsFloat throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on the Android runtime. Looking into the source code:

- SystemUtils.getJavaVersionAsFloat calls toJavaVersionIntArray with SystemUtils.JAVA_VERSION (which is obtained via getSystemProperty("java.version")).
- The method toJavaVersionIntArray splits the version String on non-digit characters and parses the parts to integers.
- Then, getJavaVersionAsFloat calls toVersionFloat, which reconstructs a float by joining parts with '.' e.g. "1.8" or "11.0".
- The exception arises on Android Dalvik VM, which might report a JAVA_VERSION string different than standard JVMs (e.g., an empty string or in a format not handled well by toJavaVersionIntArray or toVersionFloat).

The bug seems to be due to a poorly handled or unexpected Java version string on Android. For instance, if java.version is null or empty, toJavaVersionIntArray returns an empty int array (safe); however, if the version string contains unusual characters or empty splits, it might cause issues downstream trying to parse or reconstruct the float version.

Therefore, the root cause is that SystemUtils.toVersionFloat or toJavaVersionIntArray does not robustly handle the android java.version format which is causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException or parsing errors.

In particular, the toJavaVersionIntArray method splits on non-digit characters and assumes proper numeric parts. Given an unusual version string in Android environment, this leads to an invalid parse attempt or accessing invalid indexes in the float conversion step.

This diagnosis aligns with the test failure on testJavaVersionAsInt which calls SystemUtils.toJavaVersionInt with potentially null or unexpected strings and expects a safe result (0 for null). The bug report replication on Android points to the underlying SystemUtils Java version parsing logic being the root cause.

Thus the bug is in the parsing and conversion methods handling java version strings not robustly for all runtime environments, especially Android.

Recommended locations to fix will be the methods handling parsing and float conversion of the java version string.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
